documents.author: obstetrics
documents.body:
OBSTETRICS - PRENATAL VISIT
Date: 06/19/2026, 35w0d
Re: Monica Krause, DOB 02/10/1994. cc: primary care

Routine visit. BP on arrival 142/92. Asymptomatic: no headache, no visual changes, no RUQ or epigastric pain. Good fetal movement. Kept in the office for observation and labs; repeat BP four hours later 140/90.

Urine protein/creatinine ratio 0.12. Platelets, creatinine, AST and ALT all normal.

Assessment: gestational hypertension, mild range, no proteinuria and no severe features. Her mother had preeclampsia.

Plan:
- Diet changes reviewed: less sodium and processed food, regular meals.
- Home BP cuff, check twice daily, call for 160/110 or higher, headache, vision change or RUQ pain.
- Weekly visits with BP and labs as needed.
- Delivery at 37 weeks: induction scheduled for 07/08/2026 (37w5d).
- Preeclampsia warning signs reviewed; she will go to labor and delivery with any of them, or with labor.

Obstetrics

Date of service: 07/05/2026, arrival 06:20
Patient: Monica Krause, 32F

Pregnancy has been followed by her OB and is notable for mild gestational hypertension without proteinuria, which has been managed with diet. Induction had been planned for later this week. documents.title: Obstetric Discharge Summary
documents.author: obstetrics
documents.body:
OBSTETRIC DISCHARGE SUMMARY
Admitted 07/05/2026 07:05 from the emergency department. Discharged 07/07/2026.
Patient: Monica Krause, G2P2002

Admission diagnosis: term labor, 37w2d; gestational hypertension, mild, without proteinuria.
Discharge diagnoses: precipitous labor; spontaneous vaginal delivery at term; gestational hypertension.

Course: arrived on L&D contracting regularly. Cervical change was very rapid after arrival and she delivered a healthy infant by spontaneous vaginal delivery at 08:22, about two hours after she came into the ED. Labor was recorded as precipitous. Perineum intact. Placenta delivered spontaneously and complete. Blood loss within normal limits. GBS negative, no antibiotics needed. Infant went to the newborn nursery with routine care.

Postpartum: blood pressure highest 136/86, no antihypertensive needed. No headache or visual symptoms. Ambulating, voiding, tolerating diet. CBC on admission normal.

Discharge medications: prenatal vitamin daily.
Allergies: NKDA.

Follow-up: BP check in one week (primary care has agreed to see her); postpartum visit with OB at 6 weeks. Return for BP 160/110 or higher, severe headache, vision change, chest pain, shortness of breath, heavy bleeding or fever.

Obstetrics

Monica Krause, G2P2002, s/p precipitous SVD 07/05/2026 at 37w2d.

Recovering well. Bleeding stopped. Mood good; depression screening negative. Infant thriving.
BP 118/76. Home readings normal for several weeks.

Assessment: normal postpartum course. Gestational hypertension resolved.
Plan: return to routine gynecologic care; Pap due 2027. History of gestational hypertension raises long-term cardiovascular risk - recommend yearly BP and periodic lipid screening with primary care.
